name: malformed-config
description: The web service won't start after a config change — it's crashing on startup and is down. Get it serving again.
bugs: config/settings.json has a trailing comma after the last key, so it is not valid JSON and json.loads raises JSONDecodeError on startup — the visible crash

effective_config() merges the layers in the wrong precedence: it does cfg = dict(settings) then cfg.update(defaults), so the shipped defaults.json clobbers the operator's settings.json instead of the other way around. The effective request_timeout silently comes from defaults (5) instead of the operator's settings (30)

regression_check.cmd: REQUEST_TIMEOUT= python3 -c "import os,sys; os.environ.pop('REQUEST_TIMEOUT',None); sys.path.insert(0,'.'); import app; c=app.effective_config(); assert c['request_timeout']==30, ('effective request_timeout='+str(c['request_timeout'])+', operator settings.json (30) was shadowed by defaults.json (5)'); assert c['port']==8080, c['port']; assert c['log_level']=='info', c['log_level']"

correct_diagnosis: config/settings.json had a trailing comma (invalid JSON, the visible startup crash), and effective_config() merged the layers backwards — it started from settings and then called cfg.update(defaults), so the shipped defaults clobbered the operator's overrides and the effective request_timeout was 5 instead of 30. Fixing the JSON and inverting the merge so settings override defaults resolves both.

reference_fix.description: Make settings.json valid JSON and fix effective_config() so operator settings override the shipped defaults (start from defaults, then apply settings).
reference_fix.cmd:
cat > config/settings.json <<'EOF'
{
  "port": 8080,
  "workers": 4,
  "request_timeout": 30,
  "log_level": "info"
}
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('app.py')
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('    cfg = dict(settings)\n    cfg.update(defaults)  # layer the two config files', '    cfg = dict(defaults)\n    cfg.update(settings)  # operator settings override the shipped defaults')
p.write_text(s)
PY

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: only fix the JSON syntax error (remove the trailing comma). The service starts and prints its config (success condition passes), but the wrong-precedence merge is untouched, so the effective request_timeout is still the defaults' 5 instead of the operator's 30 — the held-out regression fails.
